lead: Rhode Island's dense cities, triple-deckers and oil heat shape its fire damage. SootMend helps homes and businesses from Providence to Warwick and Newport recover from fire, smoke and soot.
risk: fires in triple-deckers and older homes, oil furnace puff-backs, and kitchen fires
why: Providence, Pawtucket, Central Falls and Woonsocket have many triple-deckers and two-families built before 1940. They share stairs, walls and porches, so one fire can displace several families. Old wiring and balloon framing let fire and smoke move inside walls.

About a quarter of Rhode Island homes still heat with fuel oil, so puff-backs are a common winter call. Coastal homes in Newport and South County face salt air, which makes soot more corrosive on metal fixtures and electronics.
tips: Keep porches and back stairs clear in multi-family homes.
Have oil burners serviced every year.
Test smoke alarms in every unit monthly.
Clean soot from metal and electronics quickly near the coast.
insurance: Coastal homes may have separate hurricane deductibles, but fire and smoke claims fall under the regular deductible, so check which one applies.
areas: Providence, Warwick, Cranston, Pawtucket, East Providence, Newport and South County are all covered.

faq.q: How long does it take to fix a triple-decker after a fire?
faq.a: It depends on the damage, permits and insurance approval. A unit with smoke damage only may take a few weeks. Fire in the walls or roof can take several months, with all three units affected.
